question.problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a dilation.  Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}-35 \\ -25\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -5\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
We can write $T(v)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-35 \\ -25\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}v\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $T(v)=\frac{1}{5}v,$ and so the linear transformation $T$ is a dilation with scale factor $k=\frac{1}{5}.$

The matrix that represents a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$
